whyThisShow: This is a four-set night at the Fillmore East that captures the Dead and the New Riders of the Purple Sage sharing a stage, and the combination is what makes it canonical. One reviewer called it the kind of show where "people talk about years afterward and say 'I was there, best concert I ever saw'" [source: 'people talk about years afterward and say "I was there, best concert I ever saw."']. The show landed the same month Workingman's Dead was released, and one listener put it plainly: "It's like hearing the Workingman's album live!" [source: "It's like hearing the Workingman's album live!"]. The NRPS material — "Last Lonely Eagle, All I Ever Wanted, Henry" — drew special praise even from a self-described non-country listener [source: 'Last Lonely Eagle, All I Ever Wanted, Henry. . . hauntingly beautiful (and I don't even like country music, but this is special)']. The show was eventually released officially as Road Trips Vol. 3 No. 3, and reviewers were anticipating that outcome years before it happened [source: 'I heard a rumor they were going to release this show'].
listenFor: The acoustic early set is the first thing multiple listeners reach for: one reviewer described the first disc as something they found themselves "just playing the first disc over and over and over" [source: 'I find myself just playing the first disc over and over and over']. Pigpen is a specific draw, with one listener calling him "absolutely on fire during the Rub and Lovelight" [source: 'Pigpen is in such fine form this night, absolutely on fire during the Rub and Lovelight']. The Dark Star in the late show has a structural curiosity worth noting — it includes "about 30 seconds of near silence after the first verse" [source: 'a nice Dark Star that includes about 30 seconds of near silence after the first verse']. One reviewer singled out the Black Peter and Cumberland Blues as standouts [source: 'The Black Peter, Cumberland and Morning Dew stand out for me']. The SBD recording draws consistent praise, described as "crystal clear, crisp and bright" [source: 'The sound on this bootleg is crystal clear, crisp and bright'], though a few cuts and edits in some numbers are noted [source: 'There are a few cuts in some numbers, that's all that brings it down'].
context: May 15, 1970 at the Fillmore East was a double-bill evening with the New Riders of the Purple Sage opening and sitting in, giving the night four sets total. The era is early-70s, right at the hinge point when the Dead were moving into the acoustic/electric format that produced Workingman's Dead. The recording circulates as a soundboard (identifier: gd70-05-15.early-late.sbd.97.sbeok.shnf) and was eventually released officially on Road Trips Vol. 3 No. 3. One reviewer noted the Archive has a habit of pulling full shows once a portion goes commercial, and urged listeners to grab the NRPS material before it disappeared [source: 'The Archive has a nasty habit of removing an ENTIRE show once a PART of it has been released commercially'].
funFact: The stage banter includes an introduction where someone promises to "evoke your collective sense of piouty," to which Jerry adds "we're going to end this set, right here and now" [source: '"we\'re going to evoke your collective sense of piouty" to which Jerry adds "we\'re going to end this set, right here and now."'].
headline: Fillmore East, May '70, four sets deep.
